# Off Topic - They're up. Stand by til Sunday for photos and video.

Well, it's that time of year again.

My birthday has come and gone, and then a few days later Remembrance Day. While I completely understand there are those who put them up as early as Nov 1, and Veterans have said they fought, and some died, so we have the privilege and freedom to put them up as early as we wish, as I have family who has or is still serving in the Canadian Armed Forces (and some of my American relatives served in their Armed Forces) out of respect, as I have always done, I waited until the Remembrance Day Ceremonies had concluded before I began putting up the outdoor Christmas Decorations so it's done before the weather turns. Usually takes me 3 days. Not sure how, but I managed to get the outdoor stuff up in 2 days this year. Took a day off to rest my old achin back, hips and shoulders, and then while my wife was out this morning, I started on the indoor stuff.

It's all up now, 2750 lights and 4 lazers in the yard, 850 around the tree and in the houses of the village inside, (and I have lights left over that I had nowhere to put'em. I'll have to work on that next year. Don't like having 250 lights that didn't get put up because I had nowhere to put'em.)

IF I get my way (I can dream right😉) my wife and I will be going to watch the London Santa Claus parade tomorrow night and I'll be taking some photos/videos of that IF we do go, so I'm not planning to post the photos/videos until Sunday. Besides, while they are on right now, there's no sense posting the video of the outside stuff when I won't start pumpin the Christmas music I have out into the yard while the lights and lazers are on until Sunday as that's when I told the neighbor I'd begin to do that.

The CPKC Holiday Train will be in London on the 21st from 20:30-21:00 at the Richmond St crossing downtown I'm planning to attend that as well and hoping my wife will join me. (again I can dream right) It stays in London that night in the CPKC yard after the show, then heads to Chatham and Windsor on the 22nd. As always, there are TWO CPKC Holiday Trains. One that stays exclusively in Canada, the other, (the one that comes to those places listed above) will cross into the US after making its stops in Chatham and Windsor.

Before getting to London the Holiday Train makes stops in Cambridge/Galt at 10 Macolm St from 16:15-16:45, Ayr at Inglis Street & Willison Street 17:30-18:00, Woodstock at 199 Winniett Street from 18:50-19:10. Entertainment at all 4 stops, Cambridge through to London will be Magic! and MARIS.

Here are the links that show where each train is going, when they're expected to be there, and who the entertainment at each stop will be. They begin their journey's on November 19th.

# Fishing Report - Nanticoke- The Afternoon Shift

[![SkinnyTiller](https://cdn.longpoint.on.ca/data/avatars/m/10/10003.jpg?1754179816)](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/skinnytiller.10003/)

Been wondering last 10 days if that was all she wrote- with the Colborne buoy @8:30 matching yesterday's forecast, apparently not. Surprised by # of trucks at Hoovers pullin in. Getting ready to launch 11:30ish and lo and behold, there's [@jammer](https://www.longpoint.on.ca/members/15/) pullin up to the dock! Got some good intel, a good handshake and a chance to chew the fat for a bit 👍👍 Off we headed in separate directions, me to 25fow dropping P10s and Husky Jerks off boards.

Slow going for ~2hrs, marking very little and no interest so switched to RRFs/Gibbs/P10s off Dipsys but still no luck- threw out the old jointed Rapala that caught the last fish last trip- 1st fish 45fow off SE corner of the Shoal. Trolled over to the S side of the Shoal where the screen came to life- did 3 E-W passes following 51-58' contour. Put out blue-jointed Rapala late in the game which caught 2nd, then 3rd on the reset. Wind and chop picked up a bit out of ENE but kept speed 2.1-2.6mph with help of bowmount. Pulled lines 4:20 on a double- 1st in was 19 1/2 but gill-hooked so had to let the 2nd @23" go, in the middle of November! Managed 7/8 off Dipsys out 71 on 1 & 3 (⬇️ 32/40')- blue 4/5 on the 3 setting, yellow 3/3..... Thank you Miss Erie 👌

Combination of harnesses and cranks early then just cranks. Kept lure 15-25ft down. Lots of floating algae fowling things up. I have some trolling rudders that I put between my mainline and the leader, that cured the problem and kept the lures clean.

The Ontario Commercial Fisheries' Association (OCFA) has raised alarms regarding a steep drop in Lake Erie's Yellow Perch population, prompting calls for expanded research and management adjustments.

Key Details of the Decline

*   **Population Drop:** Yellow Perch numbers in Lake Erie have fallen by roughly 20%, hitting lows not seen since the mid-1990s. Commercial harvests have dropped from over 7 million pounds in 2016 down to about 3.1 million pounds.
*   **Quota Reductions:** In response to the slump, the multi-jurisdictional Lake Erie Committee lowered the (TAC) total allowable catch quota to **1.984 million kilograms** for 2026, down from 2.666 million kilograms in 2025.
*   **Impact on Industry:** Lake Erie accounts for 80% of Ontario's commercial fishing revenue (generating over $200 million annually), leaving commercial crews and local fish processors facing acute supply shortages.

Primary Causes

*   **Record Walleye Predation:** Lake Erie is experiencing a historic surge in Walleye (estimated at 50 to 100 million fish annually since 2020). With traditional forage fish like Rainbow Smelt and Emerald Shiners declining, large Walleye have increasingly preyed upon juvenile and larval Yellow Perch.
*   **Poor Recruitment:** Consecutive years of weak "year-classes" mean young Perch are not surviving in high enough numbers to replace aging adult fish, hindered by unstable spring temperatures and shifting plankton levels.
*   **Environmental Stress:** Climate-driven lake warming and agricultural nutrient runoff have expanded oxygen-depleted dead zones in the Central Basin, shrinking the cool, mid-depth habitats that Yellow Perch require.
*   **Predatory Birds:** Double-crested Cormorant populations along the shoreline have grown significantly, adding localized predation pressure.

**AI Overview:**

**Yes, both baitfish and Walleye move into the shallows at night in Lake Erie.**

**Why Baitfish and Walleye Move Shallow**

*   **Baitfish Movement:** Schools of baitfish—such as gizzard shad, emerald shiners, and minnows—move toward the shoreline, breakwalls, piers, and shallow flats at dusk and after dark to feed or find refuge.
*   **Walleye Behavior:** Walleyes have specialized eyes with a reflective layer (tapetum lucidum) that gives them superior low-light and night vision. They leave deeper open water or mid-basin suspensions to hunt active baitfish in skinny water (often 15 feet or less, and sometimes just 1 to 5 feet deep).
*   **Seasonal Peaks:** This "night bite" is particularly strong during the autumn cooling period (from late summer through fall and into early winter) when water temperatures drop and large female walleyes stage near shorelines.

**Where and How to Target Them**

*   **Hotspots:** Focus on rocky points, shallow reefs, harbor mouths, breakwalls, beaches, and current-moving channels.
*   **Effective Lures:** Anglers casting from shore, waders, or piers typically use slim stickbaits, shallow-running minnow baits, and rattling crankbaits (like Rapala Husky Jerks, Bomber Long-As, or Smithwick Rogues) with subtle glow or high-contrast finishes.

As I've said before, I REALLY don't care what the commerical fishery is crying about. Comparing what they're allowed to take vs what we are, and the means by which each is permitted to catch what we take, is like comparing a ping pong ball to a bowling ball. The rules and regs are completely different for them than they are for us as well, so the comparison is not equal.

They can and do take FAR more than we ever could yet they complain the most and the loudest about their inability to maintain '_what used to be_' in terms of their catch and they really could care less about the sportfishery and people like us because they're in it for profit. It's how they make their living, while we aren't allowed to legally sell what we catch. Again, the comparison is not equal.

_'What used to be'_ is in the past, and while the memories of '_what used to be_' should be remembered, '_what used to be'_ should also be left where it belongs, in the past, because its now, not then.

As I say all the time to people on the pier, if you expect it to be they way '_it used to be_' then you're not living in reality, because it isn't what '_used to be_.' It's what IS today, and as I've said, until/unless the MNR changes the daily and possession limits for us, the sportfishermen/women, then I see no need to be overly concerned that the commercial fishery is having just as much trouble finding them in the central basin as we are. They've moved. They do that. What's happening in the central basin has happened before. It'll happen again. WE have to adapt, and we haven't.

But, based on the reports I see almost daily on FB, as I said before, maybe that means, go west, and if you're up for it, to the US side of the western basin of the lake. THAT is where they are being caught in large numbers of decent sized fish.
